correctness.rationale: Every finite core with maximum degree two decomposes into paths/cycles; exact base values and disjoint-union equality yield sigma(H). The clique-first coloring picks each clique vertex’s favorite unused color and stably colors H with the remaining named colors, so all possible envy arcs involving the clique follow a strict acyclic order toward earlier clique vertices. Clique lower bounds settle sigma one and two. For sigma three, a triangle yields a clique or H contains P4 as a subgraph; path colors (1,2,3,1) and clique colors 4 through t+3 give a proper Grundy t+3 coloring. The primary established Grundy inequality plus non-induced subgraph monotonicity yields the matching lower bound. Verified certificate code checks t=1..15 and exhaustive small-profile cases; the proof handles all parameters.

value.rationale: The natural operation of adjoining a dominating clique connects resource-allocation stability to standard fan and wheel families. The result is a complete exact infinite classification for arbitrary unions of paths/cycles with any dominating clique size, identifying sharp stability premia and the exceptional P4/triangle boundary. In particular even cycles use non-induced subgraph monotonicity, and odd-cycle cones are not covered by the sharp orientation method on the base cycle. It gives genuinely new exact objects rather than a numeric recomputation or cosmetic renaming of the originating base values.
